scenario.title: 「你平常喜歡做什麼？」
scenario.context: 聊興趣是從客套進到真正聊天的轉折點。這個單元學怎麼自然地說自己喜歡什麼、最近迷上什麼、想學什麼，也順便搞懂動詞後面到底要接 to V 還是 V-ing。

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.en: So what do you like to do in your free time?

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: I'm really into pottery these days. I started taking classes last month.
lines.zh: 我最近很迷陶藝，上個月開始上課。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Harder than it looks. I keep making bowls that look like ashtrays.
lines.zh: 比看起來難。我做的碗一直很像菸灰缸。

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.en: Ha! I'd love to try it someday.
lines.zh: 哈！我有一天也想試試看。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: You should! What about you? Any hobbies?
lines.zh: 你應該試試！那你呢？有什麼嗜好？

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.en: I'm a bit of a film buff. I try to watch at least one old movie every weekend.
lines.zh: 我算是個電影迷，每個週末至少會看一部老電影。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Nice. Any recommendations? I want to watch more classics.
lines.zh: 不錯。有推薦的嗎？我想多看一些經典片。

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.en: Oh, don't get me started. I could geek out about this all day.
lines.zh: 喔，別讓我開始講，這個我可以講一整天。

lines.speaker: Jess
lines.en: Why do you look so tired?

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.en: I stayed up till 3 playing this new game. I'm totally hooked on it.
lines.zh: 我玩一款新遊戲玩到三點，完全上癮了。

lines.speaker: Jess
lines.en: You need to stop doing that on work nights.
lines.zh: 你平日晚上真的不能再這樣了。

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.en: I know, I know. I keep telling myself one more round.
lines.zh: 我知道我知道，我一直跟自己說再一局就好。

lines.speaker: Jess
lines.en: Have you thought about picking up a hobby that doesn't involve a screen?
lines.zh: 你有想過培養一個不用看螢幕的嗜好嗎？

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.en: Actually, I've been meaning to learn to swim.

lines.speaker: Jess
lines.en: Do it! I enjoy swimming. We can go together.
lines.zh: 去學！我很喜歡游泳，我們可以一起去。

patterns.en: What do you like to do in your free time?
patterns.note: 比 What's your hobby? 自然很多

patterns.en: I'd love to try it someday.
I'm not very good at it, but I enjoy it.
patterns.zh: 我不太厲害，但我很享受。

patterns.en: How did you get into it?
It's a great way to unwind.

patterns.zh: 別讓我開始講（不然會講不完）。

chinglish.wrong: My hobby is watching movies and listening music.
chinglish.right: I love watching movies, and I listen to a lot of music.
chinglish.why: My hobby is… 很像作文開頭，聊天很少這樣說。另外 listen 後面要加 to。

chinglish.right: I like going hiking. / I like to go hiking.
chinglish.why: 兩個動詞不能直接連在一起，第二個要變 V-ing 或 to V。
enjoy 後面只能接 V-ing，這是要背的。
複習第 13 單元：感興趣用 interested in。

grammar.title: 動名詞 vs 不定詞 I
grammar.oneLiner: 有些動詞後面只能接 V-ing，有些只能接 to V，有些兩個都可以。最常用的那幾個要直接背起來。
whenToUse: 只接 V-ing：enjoy, finish, mind, keep, practice, avoid, suggest, can't stand。I enjoy swimming.
只接 to V：want, need, decide, plan, hope, learn, would like, would love, try (嘗試努力)。I want to learn.
兩個都可以、意思幾乎一樣：like, love, hate, start, begin, prefer。I like cooking. = I like to cook.
介系詞後面一律接 V-ing：good at drawing, interested in learning, instead of going。
V-ing 也可以當主詞：Swimming is good exercise.
grammar.whyWeGetItWrong: 中文動詞可以直接串在一起：「喜歡去爬山」「決定開始學畫畫」。英文兩個動詞相遇時，第二個一定要變形（to V 或 V-ing），而且選哪一個要看前面的動詞。沒有完美的邏輯規則，最有效的方法是記住最常用的十幾個動詞。

examples.correct: I really enjoy cooking for friends.
examples.incorrect: I really enjoy to cook for friends.

examples.correct: I started running last year. / I started to run last year.

examples.note: 介系詞 at 後面接 V-ing。

examples.correct: Do you mind closing the window?
examples.incorrect: Do you mind to close the window?

quiz.question: Have you finished ___ (read) that book yet?
I'm not very good at ___.
quiz.explanation: 介系詞 at 後面接 V-ing。

slang.usage: be into + 名詞 / V-ing。I'm into jazz. 也可以說喜歡某個人：I think he's into you（他好像喜歡你）。

risk.note: 講興趣完全安全；講人時帶戀愛意味，看語境。

examples.en: I'm really into bouldering right now.
What kind of music are you into?

slang.meaning: 講到熱愛的東西就停不下來、宅魂爆發
slang.usage: geek out about / over something，對某事表現出極度熱情。

risk.note: 通常是友善的自嘲或調侃。

examples.en: We spent an hour geeking out about fonts.
examples.zh: 我們聊字體聊到宅魂爆發，聊了一小時。

examples.en: Sorry, I'm geeking out. I just love this stuff.
examples.zh: 抱歉我太激動了，我就是超愛這個。

slang.usage: 放在名詞後面：a film buff, a history buff, a wine buff。指對某領域很有研究的愛好者。

risk.note: 中性偏正面。注意 buff 當形容詞是「肌肉發達」，意思完全不同。

examples.en: My dad's a history buff. He's read every book about WWII.
examples.zh: 我爸是歷史迷，二戰的書他全看過。

examples.en: As a film buff, he hates it when people talk during movies.
examples.zh: 身為電影迷，他超討厭別人看電影時講話。

slang.usage: 像被魚鉤鉤住一樣戒不掉。be / get hooked on + 名詞。

risk.note: 講遊戲、影集、食物都沒問題；也可用在毒品等負面上癮，看語境。

examples.en: I got hooked on this K-drama and watched it in two days.
examples.zh: 我迷上這部韓劇，兩天就看完了。

examples.en: Be careful. That bubble tea is easy to get hooked on.
examples.zh: 小心，那家珍奶很容易上癮。

review.question: The lecture was two hours long and really ___.
review.explanation: 複習第 13 單元：造成無聊感的東西用 -ing。

review.question: She's famous, but she's really down-to-___.
review.explanation: 複習第 13 單元：down-to-earth = 實在、不做作。

review.question: Which is correct?
options: I have last night sent it.
review.explanation: 複習第 12 單元：有明確過去時間用過去式。

review.question: Let's grab coffee and catch ___. It's been ages!
review.explanation: 複習第 10 單元：catch up = 敘舊。

review.question: There are only ___ tickets left. Book now!
review.explanation: 複習第 6 單元：可數用 a few。

review.question: Which is the most natural way to ask about hobbies?
options: What do you like to do in your free time?
review.explanation: What do you like to do in your free time? 最自然。
